PullRequest.Title: chat: Copilot Fusion design fixtures: who did what, credits per model, plain wording

**Design proposal, drawn with the real chat components. No product code changes.** The only file is a Component Explorer fixture, `chat/fusionUx`. The real change comes in a follow-up PR, once we agree on the design.

## Why

In a Copilot Fusion turn, several models work on one answer: one answers, another reviews, sometimes one fixes. Today VS Code doesn't clearly say who did what, or what each model cost, and it uses internal names like "Main pass" and "Cascade workflow".

The GitHub app fixed the same problems in its Copilot Fusion UI. This PR takes the same ideas and fits them into VS Code's existing UI, without copying the GitHub app's layout.

## The GitHub app's 4 changes, and VS Code

| GitHub app change | How the GitHub app does it | VS Code today | Proposed here |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Who did what | Hover: "Answer: Claude Opus 5.5", "Review: GPT-6 Sol". Footer: "Copilot Fusion · Multiple models" | Review and fix rows name their model, but the answer has no row. The hover lists tokens per model, with no role | Each model's role first in the hover. The footer counts the models: "2 models" |
| 2. Credits per model | Credits per model, plus the total | Only the total | Credits after each role in the hover |
| 3. "Switched to X to match task complexity" only in Standard | Fixed | Already only in Standard | Nothing to do |
| 4. No internal names | "Fusion reviewed with {model}" | "Review pass", "Fix-up pass", "Preparing the Cascade workflow..." | "Reviewed with {model}", "Responding with {model}…" |

## Before and after

How to read the images: 🟥 red = what changes in VS Code today, 🟨 yellow = the GitHub app, 🟩 green = proposed. The GitHub app columns are drawn with VS Code's components, not screenshots. Click an image to see it full size.

### 1. Rows for each Copilot Fusion pass

![Pass rows: Today, GitHub app, Proposed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a66874e3-160c-44d0-b1f7-d8ce40d6afeb)

- One sentence that names the model: "Reviewed with GPT-6 Sol". Unlike the GitHub app, no "Fusion" in front: the row already sits inside a Copilot Fusion answer.
- The verdict follows: "· Approved", "· Changes requested". Today the check mark only means the pass ran.
- A running row says what it's doing ("Using a tool") instead of repeating its name.

### 2. Status line while it works, and problem messages

![Status line: Today, GitHub app, Proposed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15b7da62-ebcf-4283-a282-2e4cc1884fd1)

- Say which model is working, with no internal names: "Responding with Claude Opus 5.5…", "Handing off to GPT-6 Sol for review…".
- Problem messages say what happened to the answer: "Review by GPT-6 Sol failed; kept the answer from Claude Opus 5.5". No raw ids like `gpt-6-sol`.
- The GitHub app's wording only covers running passes; VS Code also needs the start, tools and errors.

### 3. Footer and its "Response details" hover

![Footer and hover: Today, GitHub app, Proposed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f931f13c-7180-4170-ab07-aa6fe2780ae0)

- The footer keeps the level and the credits, and adds "2 models" only when 2 or more models ran a Copilot Fusion pass.
- The hover keeps today's "Response details" and token lists. Each model line becomes "Role: model · credits", for example "Answer: Claude Opus 5.5 · 29.1 credits".
- We keep VS Code's hover rather than the GitHub app's table, because it already shows the tokens for each model.

### 4. Edge cases

![Edge cases: today's hover next to the proposed one](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e1af65e-f88b-4b3e-9e14-7bb680b2fbff)

- **One model, two jobs.** Claude Opus 5.5 answered and later applied the review's fixes. Tokens are counted per model, so it gets one line: "Answer and fix: Claude Opus 5.5 · 33.9 credits". This happens for real: the fix pass runs on the answering model.
- **Draft, review, revision.** The revision writes the final text, so the roles are "Draft", "Draft review" and "Revision", not "Answer".
- **Subagent and summary models.** They get labels ("Subagent:", "Summary:"), but they don't count toward "N models".
- **Review failed, or changes requested but not applied.** A warning stays next to the answer. Today this folds into "Completed N steps" and looks like a clean success.

### 5. Unchanged: one model, or not Copilot Fusion

![Unchanged cases](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b862aea-1f7c-42d4-b55e-f98d28d35443)

- A Copilot Fusion turn where only one model ran, and normal chats with one or several models: footer and hover stay exactly as today.

## For the follow-up PR

These came up while reviewing the code. The real change has to handle them:

- **Missing data.** The host doesn't send the answer pass today, and pass data has no kind (answer, review, fix…), verdict or credits (`IFusionPhaseMeta`, `copilotFusionProgress.ts`). The host has to add these as optional fields, and restored chats have to rebuild them.
- **Per-model totals include more than Fusion passes.** They also cover subagent, summary and image models, and sometimes a synthetic `hydrafusion-*` id. Count only pass models, label the others, and drop the synthetic line.
- **Status line.** It is removed once answer text appears, and pass rows count as "1 subagent running". Keep the status row, and don't count passes as subagents.
- **Hidden routed model.** Hover and status text must follow the existing setting that hides the routed model on Standard turns.
- **Steering message mid-run.** It moves the run to a new turn, so the footer falls back to "High". Stamp the level on the moved passes.
- **Where text is built.** Build status text on the client (localized, with display names), not on the host. Use one naming function for models in rows, hover and footer.
- **Accessibility.** Put roles inside `formatResponseTokenStats`, so the footer's ARIA label includes them, and add model and verdict to the accessible view.
- **Already fine:** switching Copilot Fusion → one model → Copilot Fusion (all Fusion state resets each turn), Copilot Fusion Standard, normal and older chats, and other agent hosts.

## How to test

1. `./node_modules/.bin/component-explorer serve -p ./test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json`
2. Open the folder `chat/fusionUx` and start with `0_StartHere`. Folders 1 to 3 are Today, GitHub app and Proposed side by side; folder 4 holds the edge cases.

Validation, run locally:

- `./node_modules/.bin/component-explorer render --project ./test/componentFixtures/component-explorer.json --fixture-id-regex 'fusionUx.*Light$'` (what the component fixtures CI renders): **passed**, 18 fixtures, 0 errors.
- `pnpm run oxlint src/vs/workbench/test/browser/componentFixtures/chat/fusionUx.fixture.ts`, plus the pre-commit hygiene hook: **passed**.
- `tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json`: **no errors in the new file**. After rebasing on `main`, other agent host files fail locally because `@microsoft/copilot-sdk` 2.0.1 couldn't be installed; this is unrelated to this change.

Model names, times and credits in the fixtures are made-up examples. No issue is linked yet.

Scenarios.Scenario: Discover and render the new Fusion design fixtures in Component Explorer or screenshot tooling
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing defineComponentFixture wrapper awaits theme/icon setup and syntax-highlighter acquisition before invoking the fixture render. Rendering must finish before fixture readiness. Module-level example formatting operates only on fixed, small arrays.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch the default Seti icon-theme JSON from the fixture server; built-in color-theme JSON is supplied from imported modules.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful cold icon-theme fetch per page, shared across fixtures through a WeakMap of promises. Warm and simultaneous renders reuse the same promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This new fixture did not exist. Existing fixtures already used the same setup and shared icon-theme promise; the PR adds no new icon-theme key or per-turn requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by setupTheme before fixture rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load Oniguruma WASM through an asynchronous XMLHttpRequest and initialize the tokenizer library.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful cold WASM request per page, coalesced by onigLibPromise. Warm renders reuse the promise; failures clear it for subsequent retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing fixtures already acquired this same cached WASM dependency. The new fixture calls the unchanged wrapper without adding a library instance or request per model or turn.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited during shared syntax-highlighter initialization before render.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the existing fixed TextMate grammar set from fixture-server resources.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared tokenizer initialization for overlapping fixture lifetimes, with grammar loads for seven configured languages and their dependencies. Initialization is recreated after the last reference is disposed; no requests scale with Fusion token counts or rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All existing component fixtures use this same reference-counted setup. The PR adds fixture executions, not a new grammar set or a change to cache ownership or scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Grammar creation uses Promise.all and is awaited before fixture rendering.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: 18 logical examples, each exposing Dark and Light variants: 36 selectable fixtures. A selected chat example has at most five turns; folder rendering can mount several examples together.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Explorer UI may render independent fixtures concurrently, as documented in defineComponentFixture. Resource initialization is coalesced. Within each renderVariant, turns are awaited sequentially. Actual screenshot-worker concurrency is controlled outside the changed file.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Color/icon theme promise caches share successful and in-flight initialization. Tokenizer acquisition coalesces overlapping fixtures and releases its instance at zero references. WASM remains shared across sequential renders. Existing failure behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: complete diff and wrapper, resource loader, tokenizer, and promise-cache implementations were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No measured render durations or screenshot-worker parallelism; those do not establish an actionable regression in this bounded fixture addition.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: this adds bounded test examples using unchanged initialization and caches. It does not introduce per-turn resource fan-out or affect product startup.

Scenarios.Scenario: Inspect running and completed Fusion pass rows, status messages, and failure notices
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After shared setup, renderVariant creates one service collection and renderTurn creates a model, view model, renderer, and template per example turn. Progress is assembled before publication; the publisher forwards all started Fusion phases together, then the completed turn is explicitly rerendered once.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Pass-row examples have five turns with at most two phase rows each. Status examples have two or five turns, with at most three fixed notices in their final turn. There is no streamed or user-sized input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Turns are constructed sequentially. The publisher calls the sink once for the ready batch, not once per phase; explicit rendering occurs once for running turns and twice for completed turns. Existing component layout scheduling remains unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No request/result cache is needed for synthetic data. toolCallStateToInvocation marks phases hasStarted:true, so AgentHostSubagentProgress neither queues delayed subagent discovery nor repeatedly republishes them. Shared setup caches are accounted for separately.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced adapter phase metadata, publisher batching, renderer cleanup, and fixture service mocks.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual browser layout/animation cost is unmeasured; the fixed example sizes do not support a high-confidence performance finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. These are display-only tool invocations, not tool execution: the adapter sets phase presentation with no chat resource and isChatAvailable:false. Tool, utility-model, title-generation, file, and agent-host services are mocks; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or model-network operation is issued by the synthetic rows. Fixed extra rendering is not a scaling regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Inspect footer credits, model roles, and side-by-side response-detail hovers, including edge cases
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixed response-detail markdown is constructed when the fixture module is loaded. Each selected turn renders its answer/footer, then creates one or two static hover widgets using the existing markdown renderer. This happens only in Component Explorer, not in product chat rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Footer examples contain two turns and one open hover. Each of eight edge-case examples has one turn and two hovers. Model-total arrays contain one to four entries, already grouped per model, including the same-model/two-role case.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Hover construction is synchronous and bounded, following sequential turn construction. pickedHover performs one small markdown replacement per grouped model, not per token or underlying pass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Immutable markdown examples are prepared once per module and reused across theme renders. Hovers are created for the selected fixture; there is no accumulating cache of totals or per-response history.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected all example arrays, formatting code, static-hover construction, and lifecycle registration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No profiling of hover layout was available. There is no realistic unbounded cardinality or product hot-path change.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Static open hovers are intentional fixture output, and the numeric token totals do not represent allocated token arrays. Markdown contains text, inline code, lists, and a fixed table—not remote images or files. All hover widgets and rendered markdown results are owned by the fixture disposable store.

Scenarios.Scenario: Leave a fixture, rerender a theme, or run normal product Fusion/non-Fusion chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Fixture teardown disposes the context store, its services, models, view models, renderer templates, publishers, and hovers. Product chat continues on unchanged production code; the PR changes only a test fixture module.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Resource ownership is bounded by currently mounted fixture instances and their fixed turns. Product session history and number of requests do not execute the new fixture helpers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing fixture teardown handles disposal through one host-owned disposable. Renderer disposeTemplate clears rendered parts and template disposables; rerendering clears element-scoped ownership. No new cleanup queue or parallel remote disposal is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tokenizer references are released with the fixture store; shared theme/WASM keys are fixed and unchanged. MockChatService.acquireExistingSession returns undefined, so a running synthetic request does not retain a model through a product background-session cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: checked context teardown, createEditorServices disposal, renderer disposeElement/disposeTemplate, phase presentation, and mock session acquisition.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Static review cannot measure browser memory or render time; no changed ownership path or production execution path supports a concrete regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable retention or cleanup regression, and no product performance change. The proposal's Today/GitHub app/Proposed wording is fixture data, not a modification of production renderer behavior. No removed performance mechanism qualifies for regression-fix provenance reporting.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the distinct performance-review pass against ccda52f9aa46a66b92edd7a331643b690219b866, inspecting the complete one-file inventory and all diff bytes. Loaded the review guide and learned mechanisms, traced bounded fixture rendering, shared asset boundaries/cache coalescing, progress publication, and teardown. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance regression or concrete regression fix found; no findings submitted.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
